articles.title: Angry over wife's 'affair', B'luru man kills stepson, attacks spouse with knife, hammer
articles.summary: In a tragic turn of events on November 16, a man named Sudeep was arrested for the alleged murder of his wife's teenage son amidst a violent quarrel in Padmanabhanagar. The altercation left his wife, Seema, seriously injured. Neighbors, concerned about the family's escalating disputes, prompted police intervention, and they uncovered blood during a welfare check.

articles.title: 'Your own confession': Rahul, Kharge hit out at PM Modi over 'hunger' charge at India Inc
articles.summary: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge have criticised PM Modi for blaming the business community. They argue that Modi government has failed to generate adequate employment and support small businesses. PM Modi remarked on the need for industry to increase jobs and salaries amid government concessions. The Congress party asserted its role in economic liberalisation and criticised the current economic situation.

articles.title: Parl showdown 2.0? Cong says INDIA bloc, including DMK, NCP-SP, united on delimitation
articles.summary: The Congress party is voicing concerns about the government's insufficient communication about the upcoming delimitation exercise. In a show of solidarity, leaders from the INDIA coalition, including DMK and NCP-SP, have come together on vital demands for transparent consultations. Congress emphasizes the importance of maintaining existing Lok Sabha seats and ensuring an equitable distribution among states during the process.

articles.title: Owaisi-Azad alliance looks promising, but Akhilesh has little to fear: 5 reasons why
articles.summary: The Owaisi-Chandrashekhar Azad alliance may look like a major threat to Akhilesh Yadav's PDA formula, but the reality in Uttar Pradesh tells a different story. From Akhilesh's efforts to broaden the SP's support base to Azad's challenge from Mayawati and Owaisi's limited success in UP, we examine five reasons why the new Dalit-Muslim alliance may not be as big a worry for the SP chief as it appears.

articles.title: Elon Musk on working with Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa: Things will be fine
articles.summary: Elon Musk anticipates that Texas will be governed moderately under Gina Hinojosa, who recently won the election. Hinojosa has communicated her willingness to engage with Musk's companies while emphasizing Texas's interests. Her administration aims to prioritize public land preservation and maintain a strong business environment for residents. Additionally, SpaceX is interested in acquiring land near its launch site for habitat preservation.

articles.title: Mamdani unveils $290m plan to close Rikers Island by 2032, 5 years past deadline
articles.summary: In a bold move, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled a strategic initiative aimed at closing Rikers Island jail by 2032. The plan emphasizes the establishment of four smaller jails across various boroughs, with a focus on slashing the jail population. Key investments in mental health services and job training are central to this effort, as the city seeks to reform the beleaguered jail system.

articles.title: ‘Intelligent caller’ to team leader: How this call centre ran Apple gift card scam
articles.summary: In a significant crackdown, authorities in Gurgaon have apprehended 17 individuals involved in a deceptive call center scheme targeting Apple users across North America. These suspects posed as Apple customer service agents to obtain sensitive personal data. Victims were lured into buying gift cards, which were exploited for financial scams.

articles.title: Israel's new 'Super Ice' missile packs 4x the punch; why it's a perfect fit for India
articles.summary: Rafael Advanced Defense Systems has unveiled the Super Ice missile, featuring a 1,000 lb warhead for strategic strikes. This missile can be launched from various platforms, making it versatile for military applications. India has explored partnerships to manufacture Rafael's Ice Breaker missile under existing agreements. Super Ice could potentially enhance India's capability to strike hardened targets with greater effectiveness.

After more than five hours of searching, neighbor Jay Stewart found her hiding under a bush. Emergency responders ensured the girl's safety and promptly took her to a hospital for evaluation. Authorities classified this incident as a case of a wandering child.

articles.title: Florida mom buys 480 toilet rolls, earns 8,500 miles for daughter's flight home
articles.summary: In an effort to minimize travel costs, Florida resident Michelle Jolene bought toilet paper through an airline shopping website, amassing 8,500 airline miles. These miles allowed her daughter to fly home for Thanksgiving from Washington, D.C. As airfares continue to climb, families face challenges with ticket prices and possible cancellations during the holiday rush. Michelle's inventive method showcases the potential for everyday spending to alleviate travel expenses.

articles.title: Palmer Luckey explains why he wants Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO

He articulated differing views on US chip exports to China but emphasized Huang's significance. Luckey indicated that China benefits from Huang's absence, as it seeks dominance in its domestic processor industry. He further criticized Nvidia's interim leadership, asserting that it lacks Huang's understanding and relationships.

articles.title: Ponting explains PBKS' strategy behind trading for Hardik Pandya

He stressed the significance of all-rounders for adaptable strategies, believing that the inclusion of Pandya and other skilled players will elevate the team's capabilities for the next three years.

articles.title: Myanmar genocide verdict divides world, opens Pandora's box for Israel
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice's ruling on genocide has significant ramifications for Myanmar and sets a precedent for international law. This landmark verdict holds Myanmar responsible for its military actions against the Rohingya during recent conflicts. While the United States signals caution, the European Union stands in full support. Experts warn this ruling may also shape ongoing legal actions concerning Israel, particularly regarding military strategies in Gaza.

articles.title: Travis Kelce gets emotional over Arrowhead as Chiefs plan $3 billion stadium

Alongside challenging the unjust marriage bar, her relentless advocacy has left a lasting legacy. A recently unveiled bronze statue in Brisbane commemorates her monumental contributions, symbolizing the ongoing fight for equality and the empowerment of women across Australia.

articles.summary: An illustrated manuscript known as the Book of Miracles documents extraordinary natural events from the 16th century. It features 167 paintings showcasing phenomena perceived as divine warnings, including blood rain and comets. The manuscript, discovered in a German castle, is the only known surviving copy of its kind. A December auction will allow public institutions to acquire the rare volume for the first time.

The school, which serves around 560 children, has operated without owning its premises for nearly four decades. Through the initiative Dharavi Rising, Daniel seeks to highlight educational needs in the community.

This centre will specifically handle rejected asylum seekers who have exhausted all legal options to remain in Europe. The countries aim to make this facility operational by 2027 and will initially accommodate around 100 migrants. The proposed arrangement reflects a broader shift in the EU’s immigration policy and deportation strategies.

articles.title: California mother, baby died after discharge; $9.25m jury award capped

A jury subsequently awarded $9.25 million in damages, yet limitations under California's MICRA restrict non-economic compensation. This heart-wrenching case underscores the urgent necessity for reform in medical negligence laws, as the families advocate for changes to protect others from similar tragedies.

articles.title: 'Kisi ke baap ka Hindustan thodi hai’: Diljit Dosanjh takes stage despite threats
articles.summary: Despite facing threats and considerable opposition, Diljit Dosanjh took the stage in Indore to celebrate culture with his loyal fans. His performance included powerful couplets that highlighted resilience and strength, emphasizing that nothing would deter them from their cherished traditions. Although some emails threatened bomb blasts, authorities later confirmed them as hoaxes. Dosanjh's unwavering dedication showcased his commitment to his audience amidst adversity.

articles.title: Record alert! Kagiso Rabada surpasses Allan Donald in SA’s all-time wicket tally
articles.summary: Kagiso Rabada reached a remarkable career milestone by exceeding Allan Donald's wicket record, bagging five wickets to elevate his total to 606 in international cricket. Although Bangladesh faced an early struggle, they mounted a strong comeback driven by an incredible 206-run partnership between Towhid Hridoy and Litton Das, concluding the day at 327 for 6 and revitalising their innings.

articles.title: Mumbai physics forum hosts online lecture by Pakistani nuclear scientist
articles.summary: Mumbai recently held an online event to honor the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam. Eminent scientist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy delivered a lecture discussing Salam's contributions to physics and his life. Hoodbhoy highlighted Salam's significance as a symbol of goodwill between India and Pakistan. He mentioned Salam's lack of recognition in Pakistan due to his Ahmadiyya sect affiliation, affecting youth role models.

articles.title: Study of 440 female elephants finds social ties fray after population losses
articles.summary: A study in Udawalawe National Park indicates that dwindling elephant groups result in significant social vulnerabilities. With fewer individuals, elephants transition from larger communities to smaller, more isolated factions, which impairs their capacity to nurture and feed effectively. Once a critical social threshold is exceeded, the difficulty of reversing such fragmentation intensifies.

articles.title: Man finds 1,132 ancient Mexican artefacts in dumpster; students return them
articles.summary: During a house clearance in Massachusetts, over 1,100 fascinating pre-Hispanic archaeological items were rescued from a dumpster. Matthew Pioggia, noticing their historical significance, enlisted archaeologist Jeremy Pilver for help. Together with more than 40 high school students, they meticulously documented and cleaned these artifacts over nearly two years, unveiling their southeastern Mexican origins. In August 2026, the collection was respectfully returned to the Mexican Consulate in Boston.

articles.title: 62 endangered San Francisco garter snakes released into wild after zoo care
articles.summary: In a remarkable conservation effort, 62 San Francisco garter snakes, previously raised in a zoo, have been successfully released into their natural environment. This project stems from the need to ensure the species’ survival, as they were originally taken from the wild. Alongside this, restoration activities are being implemented to enhance their habitat.

articles.title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype

The current film policy is criticized for not adequately supporting local productions while favoring external filmmakers. articles.title: Watch: Forest staff chase lion on motorcycles at Gujarat safari park

An inquiry was launched, but no harassment was confirmed regarding the lion's treatment.

A permanent conservation agreement prevents non-agricultural development and preserves the land's ecological value. Additionally, a future grant will facilitate restoration work across 350 acres to control invasive grass and support biodiversity.

articles.title: 1884 Virginia school for Black children reopens as museum after $6.2m revamp

After a refurbishment costing around $6.2 million, the building now serves to educate about Black history. Initially established in 1884, it provided education to Black children during segregation until 1958. The new museum aims to preserve memories and share the stories of those associated with the school.
